summary: fast-url-utils ships encrypted payload decrypted and executed via Node by native addon on require()
details: The package advertises lightweight URL parsing but on require() loads a prebuilt native N-API addon (native.napi.node on Linux, native_win.node on Windows) that reads a shipped 1,325,877-byte opaque blob (.napi_cache, zero printable strings, sha256 f896dc12dfccbe23506159982159b3c837ad714cb7f2989358b7104e6204cc7b), writes it to a temp path (/tmp/.%u on Linux, GetTempPath on Windows), sets executable permissions, and spawns the Node interpreter on the decrypted output (execlp fork/setsid on Linux, CreateProcessA with `node "%s"` on Windows). Execution is gated on CI/build environment variables: the native binaries embed and getenv-probe GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, VELA, SCREWDRIVER, and DRONE, keeping the payload dormant on developer workstations and firing on build infrastructure that holds deployment and publishing tokens. The addon also performs anti-analysis checks: reads /proc/self/status for TracerPid:, inspects /proc/self/maps, /proc/1/cgroup and /proc/1/cmdline for docker/containerd/kubepod/podman/tini/dockerinit, searches running processes for wireshark and httpdebug, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, and CreateToolhelp32Snapshot/Process32First/Next. The stated purpose (URL parsing) has no legitimate need for an encrypted sidecar binary, a drop-and-exec loader, CI-environment gating, or debugger/container/sniffer evasion.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
